'''Isaiah Canaan''' (born May 21, 1991) is an American college basketball player. He is currently a Senior [[point guard]] at [[Murray State University]].

Canaan, a 6'0" guard from [[Biloxi, Mississippi]], went to [[Murray State Racers men's basketball|Murray State]] after leading [[Biloxi High School]] to the 5A [[Mississippi]] state championship as a senior.<ref name=MSUBIO>{{cite web| title = MSU bio| publisher = Murray State Athletics| year = 2011 | url =http://goracers.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=2471&path=mbball| accessdate = February 7, 2012}}</ref> Canaan had an instant impact for the Racers, as he averaged 10.4 [[points per game]] and led the Racers in three-point percentage at .485 as a freshman in the [[2009–10 Murray State Racers men's basketball team|2009–10 season]]. He was named 2010 [[Ohio Valley Conference]] (OVC) freshman of the year as the Racers went 17-1 in OVC play, winning the league. They also won the [[2010 Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2010 OVC tournament]]. Canaan was named tournament MVP as he scored 16 points off the bench for the Racers in the final.<ref>{{cite web| title = Murray St. gets 30th win in earning NCAA berth| publisher = ESPN.com| year = 2010 | url =http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300650093| accessdate = February 7, 2012}}</ref> Murray State went on to knock off 4-seeded [[2009–10 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] in the [[2010 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]], before losing to eventual national runner-up [[2009–10 Butler Bulldogs men's basketball team|Butler]] 54-52 in the second round.

In his sophomore year, Canaan raised his scoring average to 11.7 points per game and was named to the first team All-OVC team. He led the Racers to their second straight OVC regular-season championship. Though they lost in the [[2011 Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Tournament|2011 OVC Tournament]], the Racers again went to the postseason in the form of the [[2011 National Invitation Tournament]].

As a junior, Canaan and the Racers had a breakout season. Canaan was named to the preseason All-OVC team. Led by Canaan, Murray State began the season with a school and conference record 23 straight wins. Included was a [[2011 Great Alaska Shootout]] tournament championship, as Canaan was named MVP, scoring 36 in the tournament final.<ref>{{cite news |title= Murray State wins the Great Alaska Shootout |author= Jeremy Peters|newspaper= Anchorage Daily News |date= November 27, 2011|url=http://www.adn.com/2011/11/26/2190476/murray-state-wins-great-alaska.html |accessdate=February 7, 2012}}</ref> Canaan, the Racers' leading scorer, was named to the finalist lists for the [[Bob Cousy Award]]<ref>{{cite web| title = 2012 Cousy Award Finalists| publisher = Cousy Award| year = 2012 | url =http://www.cousyaward.com/finalists.php| accessdate = February 7, 2012}}</ref> and the [[Oscar Robertson Award]].<ref>{{cite web| title = USBWA Oscar Robertson midseason watch list| publisher = USBWA.com| year = 2012 | url =http://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2012/oscar120206.html| accessdate = February 7, 2012}}</ref>
